about: Scam SMS texts collected verbatim from published warnings and reports, for the suspicious-request classifier's calibration and final-test sets. Never use these for training. Keep texts from the same campaign_id in the same split. Collected 2026-10-09 from public sources; see source_url per message. Labels are suggestions under the suspicious-request definition and must be reviewed before use.
provenance_notes: source_kind 'official' means a government agency or the named company published or quoted the text. 'news' means a news organization quoted it. 'blog' means a personal blog or comment thread reproduced a received text; weaker provenance, decide before using in the final test. completeness 'fragment' means the article quoted only part of the message. completeness 'pattern' means an author's rendition of a documented campaign, possibly paraphrased: usable for training or calibration, not the final test. completeness 'stitched' means assembled from quoted fragments in one article: same restriction as pattern.
known_gaps: Verbatim official-provenance texts remain few; most full texts come from blogs or author patterns. Campaigns described but not quoted in official advisories (PHLPost P17.05 address-fee, LBC redelivery fee, SSS benefit-claim links, PhilHealth info-update site, Smart fake SIM re-registration, MMDA NCAP violations, BDO account-on-hold) are listed in reconstruction_candidates and may only be paraphrased for training, never for calibration or final testing.
